construction.shape: Append-only per-credential accepted chain, with amortized service-signed heads
construction.link: SHA-256( LP("done/accept/v1") || LP(workspace_id) || LP(credential_id) || LP(dec seq) || LP(dec epoch) || LP(hex digest) || LP(hex prev) )
construction.empty_chain: 32 zero bytes. Position 1 binds label, workspace and credential itself.
construction.head: Ed25519 over LP("done/accept-head/v1") || LP(workspace_id) || LP(credential_id) || LP(dec seq) || LP(hex link) || LP(dec epoch) || LP("true"|"false")
construction.signing_key: A separate acceptance-signing key, certified by the authorization key in the epoch it appears in. It is hot because it signs on the delivery path; the epoch key need not be.
construction.length_prefix: uint16be(byteLength) || utf8 — injective, so no field can shift another
client_rules: Verify a head against the link you replayed yourself, never the link the head claims.
Admit no envelope without a signed head at or above its position.
First-seen-wins per (credential, position). A second link at a held position is equivocation, and a valid signature is not an answer to it.
Above the newest head, hold rather than discard. Missing evidence is availability, not integrity (§7.5).

not_here.primitives: SHA-256 and Ed25519 KATs are row 1’s, in test/vectors/algorithm-suite.json.
not_here.wire: How a link and a head travel beside an envelope is row 4’s framing.
not_here.retention: How deep a device keeps its own chain is row 6.
not_here.checkpoint: The head vector a checkpoint manifest carries is §7.6’s, and its construction is row 7.

service.role: The acceptance-signing key. Hot, because it signs on the delivery path.

impostor.role: Not the service. Present so "signed by the wrong key" is a vector rather than a sentence.

vectors.name: first-accepted
vectors.why: Position 1 of a fresh credential. `prev` is the empty chain, so the first link still binds label, workspace and credential.

vectors.name: second-accepted
vectors.why: Position 2, same epoch. The link is the only thing carrying the fact that position 1 exists.

vectors.name: across-an-epoch
vectors.why: Position 3 references epoch 8. A genuine late-arriving old-epoch update is legitimate (§7.5), so epoch is bound per position rather than per chain.

vectors.name: other-credential-same-position
vectors.why: The phone at its own position 1, carrying the laptop’s position-1 digest. Same workspace, same position, same bytes, different chain.

heads.name: live-head-at-2
heads.why: One signature covering positions 1 and 2. This is the amortization: the chain reaches back, so the service need not sign every position.

heads.name: finalized-head-at-3
heads.why: The cutoff. `final: true` says no position above 3 will ever be accepted for this credential, which is one third of what revocation commits (§7.5).

must_fail.name: wrong-workspace
must_fail.mutate: Replay the chain under a different workspace id. An envelope accepted in one workspace is not evidence in another.

must_fail.name: wrong-credential
must_fail.mutate: Replay the laptop’s chain as the phone’s. Chains are per credential, so a position in one is not a position in the other.

must_fail.name: wrong-sequence
must_fail.mutate: Replay position 2 as position 3. A link cannot be moved along its own chain.

must_fail.name: wrong-epoch
must_fail.mutate: Replay position 2 under epoch 8. This is the field §7.5 says the epoch alone cannot carry, so it is bound where acceptance is recorded instead.

must_fail.name: wrong-digest
must_fail.mutate: Replay position 2 over a different update digest. Substituting the envelope under an accepted position is what the digest binding exists for.

must_fail.name: reordered-chain
must_fail.mutate: Compute position 3 over position 1’s link, skipping position 2. Isolates `prev`, the only field that makes the chain a chain.

must_fail.name: renumbered-link-label
must_fail.mutate: Replay under "done/accept/v2". The label is where this carrier authenticates its own version, so a renumbered chain must fail to verify rather than select another suite (row 1). **Deliberately not named `aad-only-`**: no link-layer negative can isolate one field, because eliding the head’s `link` rescues every one of them. That is the pin between the two layers, not a coverage gap — see the selection document.

must_fail.name: head-signed-by-impostor
must_fail.mutate: A well-formed head over the correct link, signed with RFC 8032 TEST 1’s key instead of the service key.

must_fail.name: head-wrong-sequence
must_fail.mutate: Verify the head as though it were signed at position 3. Isolates the head’s `seq`, which is what bounds how far the evidence reaches.

must_fail.name: head-wrong-link
must_fail.mutate: The service signed a head over a different link at this position. The client verifies against the link it replayed itself, so the signature does not open.

must_fail.name: head-wrong-workspace
must_fail.mutate: Verify the head under a different workspace id.

must_fail.name: head-wrong-credential
must_fail.mutate: Verify the laptop’s head as the phone’s. A head is per credential for the same reason the chain is.

must_fail.name: head-wrong-epoch
must_fail.mutate: Verify the head under a different epoch.

must_fail.name: head-final-flag-flipped
must_fail.mutate: Verify the live head as though it were final. **This is the finalization boundary itself**: flipped one way it freezes a still-authorized credential, the other way it keeps a revoked one’s writes admissible.

must_fail.name: forked-link-at-same-position
must_fail.mutate: A second, properly signed head over a different link at a position the client already holds. First-seen-wins per (credential, position) refuses it — the service equivocated, and a valid signature is not an answer to that.

must_fail.name: envelope-beyond-signed-head
must_fail.mutate: Position 3 offered with only the head signed at position 2. Evidence is required on every applied envelope (§7.5), so this one is held rather than applied.
